## Who the user is

The user is Imam Taufiq, also known as Imam Digmi in some online accounts. He holds an S.Kom. degree, which he uses for his thesis work. He is from Indonesia and lives in the Bogor area. His main language is Bahasa Indonesia, he works comfortably in English for technical and professional topics, and he is learning Arabic (Fusha and Saudi dialect).

He works remotely from Indonesia as a Data Engineer at Hassad Food in Qatar. The company requires physical presence in Qatar, which conflicts with working from Bogor. A Qatar role and a visa application are in progress, and their status cannot be confirmed as of October 2026. He is also pursuing an MTI (Magister Teknologi Informasi) at BINUS University, with a thesis in progress. Long-term goals include a PhD, possibly in Saudi Arabia, and publishing in Q1 or Q2 international journals. His PhD interests are data science, data engineering, computer vision, AI and remote sensing.

## Important people in his life

- Wife and child: he is married and has a child about 13–14 months old (as of September–October 2026). In October 2026 he travelled to Singapore with his wife and child for an Apple repair. When planning family travel, he considers the child's comfort and extra time needed. Family members had flu in September 2026, and the child tested positive for Influenza A that month.
- Mother: she travelled to Makkah and was due home in September 2026 (historical).
- Ustadz Abdul Wahhab, Lc., M.A.: the teacher of his Makkah & Madinah Mengaji study circle (5–7 participants). He has asked for help writing Arabic messages to this ustadz and to study friends (teman belajar).
- Work colleagues: Saad (main stakeholder and coordinator), Tahir (developer on the CRM work), Ahmed (internal project), Samer (VM and Ministry database work), Reza (visa matters), and Essam (data support for Dandy).
- Mosque: Masjid As Sakinah Nusantara (also called Nustro), where the study circle meets.

## Platforms and tools

- Telegram is his main channel for agent notifications and scheduled job output. Reports go to the Digmi Laboratorium group. Daily lessons go to topic 35, with one separate chat per topic rather than merged messages.
- Hermes Agent runs on his macOS desktop (account imamtaufiq). He manages work through kanban tasks in the Hermes CLI and delegates file changes to the agent. Hermes uses Hindsight as its memory provider.
- Hardware and OS: a Mac with Apple Silicon (he has used both NVIDIA GPUs and Apple Silicon). He also uses a Windows VM for GIS work, accessed through Windows App, and some internal organisation resources are only reachable from that office VM.
- Tools: Python, SQL and PowerShell; Azure SQL, Azure Storage Explorer, Obsidian (LLM Wiki vault), GitHub (private backups at imamdigmi/hermes, imamdigmi/memories and imamdigmi/dotfiles), chezmoi for dotfiles, Homebrew, zsh, and Terminal.app or iTerm.
- He explored connecting Hermes to WhatsApp and asked whether that needed a new phone number or SIM.

## Communication preferences

- Practical, direct and specific communication is his stated preference. Short messages suit simple items.
- For simple, factual, quiz or quick-translation questions he wants very concise answers with no padding. For complex technical problems he is willing to read long, in-depth explanations.
- He values technical accuracy above all. He prefers the assistant to admit uncertainty rather than invent information, and he is willing to correct wrong answers.
- He wants evidence-based answers, with documentation or references. For research he asks for sources from published papers and journals, and GitHub for implementation. He asked for the best-researched existing community approaches, not invented ones.
- He likes ready-to-use terminal commands, Python code and SQL queries, and concrete examples from real scenarios. He likes ASCII or Mermaid diagrams to explain technical pipelines, and copy-paste-friendly formats. Plain text is often enough for him; he does not always need a document or file.
- He prefers comparing options and understanding trade-offs (performance, cost, complexity) before deciding. He likes discussing the long-term consequences of technical decisions and favours pragmatic solutions that fit available hardware and resources. He does not want enterprise complexity when the problem scale does not justify it.
- He learns by reading concepts, trying implementations directly, debugging, comparing alternatives and asking follow-up questions. Explanations should be adjusted to this.
- For code review he wants minimal code, no speculative abstraction, concrete bugs cited as path:line, hard defects separated from optional smells, and under 400 words.
- For academic writing he wants structured text, APA 7th edition references, and a clear scientific contribution and novelty rather than a plain implementation report.
- For English professional writing he likes concise phrasing; for his CV he asked for bullet points with action verbs.
- Example of an unwanted format: for the hermes-settings-backup job report (19 Oct 2026) he asked for a shorter report containing only statistics, because the previous one was too long.

## Working rules he has set for the assistant

- Database safety: he wants approval before every database query, SELECT-only access, and any INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP or other mutation shown as a SQL code block for him to run manually, never executed by the assistant.
- Data work: keep attributes such as packaging and product state as separate fields rather than deleting them. Never convert volume to mass without a domain rule. He wants no train/test splits and no invented reviewer labels for now, and no actual deletion yet.
- Decisions: he prefers to make key decisions himself. For example, he has not yet chosen between the full taxonomy and a candidate shortlist, and he asked the assistant not to decide this for him.
- Error reporting: when a vLLM error occurs, he wants the full traceback, not only the last line, so the assistant can find the problem without trial and error.
- Installed-package changes: he prefers solutions outside installed library code (for example sitecustomize.py or flags) rather than editing library source.
- Model choice: for OCR and similar tasks he values precision over demo speed (he chose the bf16 full-precision model over the 8-bit version for thesis OCR accuracy).
- Learning content: the daily Arabic lesson should build gradually, with no repeated material. The daily computer vision lesson is one small concept per day and does not repeat topics already covered. A reset is possible by clearing the continuity history.
- He wants the assistant to support critique and validation of research results produced by agents.

## Routines and what is coming up

- Daily: 03:00 settings backup (alerts only on failure); 03:05 Hindsight backup (alerts only on failure); 09:00 computer vision lesson; 09:05 Arabic lesson (with a 7-day grammar review); 21:20 dotfiles backup. A 17 October request to move job triggers to 21:00, 21:05 and 21:15 has no confirmed record of being applied.
- Mengaji study circle: planned every other Wednesday after Maghrib (about 20:00–21:00). The schedule is still recorded as planned, not confirmed.
- Reminder due: the Masjid As Sakinah Nusantara permit letter for the Mengaji study circle is due Wednesday 21 October 2026. It must state no speakers or loudspeakers (tanpa speaker / pengeras suara) and include a photo. Submission is not confirmed. The 19 October Telegram reminder was not delivered, so it should be resent and delivery confirmed.
- Possible pickup: around 8 November 2026 a friend may bring back the repaired MacBook Pro. The repair was confirmed on 16 October and the device works normally, so pickup may no longer be needed; he has not said either way.
- Open work: review_calibration.csv for the automap pilot (he said he would review it and report back on 19 October). Work on the thesis includes OCR extraction of the BINUS thesis guideline into markdown.
- Reliability: backups are important to him because he lost a MacBook to a sudden logic-board failure and another laptop to theft, so he treats backups and setup carefully.

## Dated history and what may have changed

- 16 October 2026: the first profile facts were recorded (identity, work, interests, and communication preferences).
- 17 October 2026: he set up the Telegram-delivered daily lesson jobs and the azure-sql-query skill with approval-based access. He also asked for the dotfiles and Hindsight backup structure.
- 18 October 2026: the automap project was created in Hermes, and the thesis OCR work began.
- 19 October 2026: he approved several pilot recommendations and asked for the report format change. His 17 October instruction to move job times to 21:00–21:15 has no later record confirming it was applied, so the schedule is unresolved.
- 20 October 2026: he was working on commitment-letter PDF generation with WeasyPrint on macOS.
- Dates for the Qatar role, visa, thesis deadline and PhD plans are not confirmed in the records; the thesis deadline is only an unconfirmed estimate of around August 2026.

## Daily routine

Scheduled jobs send their output to Telegram (group "Digmi Laboratorium", topic 35; each topic is a separate chat). Times are Asia/Jakarta (+07:00):
- 03:00 hermes-settings-backup (no LLM tokens; report to Telegram)
- 03:05 hindsight-memory-backup (alerts on failure only)
- 09:00 daily-learning-computer-vision (one new small concept per day, no repeats)
- 09:05 daily-learning-arabic (one bite-sized lesson per day; concise review every 7 days)
- 21:20 dotfiles-backup (chezmoi re-add, commit, push, then Telegram notice)

On 17 Oct 2026 the user asked for the backup triggers to move to 21:00, 21:05 and 21:15. Later records still show 03:00, 03:05 and 21:20, and none confirms which applied. Treat the backup times as unresolved until confirmed. The 09:00 and 09:05 learning jobs (created 17 Oct) are the latest schedule.

The 09:00 lesson requires the Hermes gateway. After any gateway restart, confirm it is running before 09:00.

## Arabic study routine

The user is learning Fusha and Saudi 'Ammiyah step by step and already knows the letters and basic pronunciation. Each daily lesson has 3 fi'il verbs (madhi, mudhari', amr, masdar), 3 mufradat, 1 Saudi 'Ammiyah expression and a speaking challenge. Never repeat previously taught words or material.

## Weekly and recurring commitments

- Mengaji study circle (Makkah & Madinah Mengaji): planned every other Wednesday, about 20:00–21:00 after Maghrib, at Masjid As Sakinah Nusantara (Nustro), 5–7 participants, ustadz Abdul Wahhab, Lc., M.A. Status is "planned" and not confirmed.
- Wed 21 Oct 2026: mosque permit letter due. It must state no speakers or loudspeakers (tanpa speaker / pengeras suara) and include a photo. Submission not confirmed. The 19 Oct Telegram reminder was not delivered; resend it and confirm delivery.
- Around 8 Nov 2026: a friend may return the repaired MacBook Pro (repair confirmed 16 Oct). Pickup may be unnecessary; the user has not said.
- Work follow-up (from 19 Oct): review review_calibration.csv (100 candidate product pairs) and report back. No date recorded.
- MTI thesis at BINUS University: no deadline recorded. A Feb 2026 estimate of about six months implies around August 2026 (unconfirmed inference). The program has three semesters a year, two periods each.

## Schedule constraints and context

The user is married with a child about 13–14 months old and plans around family needs. In October 2026 they travelled to Singapore (Bugis) with the child for an Apple repair.

The user works remotely from Bogor, Indonesia. A Qatar role would require on-site presence, which conflicts with this. Visa and contract status cannot be confirmed as of October 2026.

Home workout equipment: barbell bar, two ~10 kg plates, two 3 kg dumbbells, resistance bands, a workout bench and a kettlebell.

## Reminders and check-ins

- Telegram is the main channel for agent notifications and all scheduled job reports.
- Backup jobs announce failures only, not routine successes.
- Resend reminders and confirm delivery; do not assume it. API status alone does not prove delivery, so the user should check the two lesson messages visually.
- Keep simple reminders short and direct, with practical, specific wording. Answer simple factual questions very briefly; complex technical topics can be long.
- Sync across devices is manual (`chezmoi update`), not cron, because auto-apply could overwrite unpushed local changes.
- Known failure: on 17 Oct 2026 Telegram delivery failed because python-telegram-bot was missing. It has since been installed.

## Open items (as of 20 Oct 2026)

The routines snapshot (19 Oct 2026) is marked stale; items were checked against raw records where possible.

Unresolved: backup trigger times (see Daily routine), whether the Mengaji schedule still holds, and whether the MacBook pickup is needed.

## Dated deadlines and promises

- **MacBook pickup, around 8 Nov 2026.** A friend returning to Indonesia was to bring back the repaired MacBook Pro (recorded 16 Oct 2026). The repair is now confirmed complete and the machine is working normally, so the pickup may no longer be needed. Confirm with the friend before 8 Nov.

- **Mengaji study group, next session Wednesday 21 Oct 2026, about 20:00–21:00** at Masjid As Sakinah Nusantara (Nustro), led by ustadz Abdul Wahhab, Lc., M.A. This is a fortnightly group, but the exact dates are not confirmed.

- **Qatar work situation, no current deadline.** Visa, contract and on-site policy were unresolved as of Oct 2026. A 2025 note warned the contract could end in December if the visa issue was not solved. No newer deadline is recorded.

## Open tasks and follow-ups

- **Automap pilot (automated product taxonomy mapping).** Final selection, row removal, dataset split and training are on hold until the user reviews the human-review batch (CSV review, about 100 pairs). Decisions still open: full taxonomy versus candidate shortlist, how conflicting English labels are adjudicated, and whether diversity selection ignores package and size. The restart record is Process/005, dated 19 Oct 2026.

- **Assistant-offered work awaiting the user's go-ahead.** (a) An AGENTS.md navigation pointer for the automap project was blocked by a protected-file policy and needs separate human approval. (b) A text-to-SQL catalog file and two introspection scripts were offered on 17 Oct and are still awaiting confirmation. (c) A browser fix was offered for live research sources, pending go-ahead.

- **Hermes GPG backup passphrase.** Copy it from the macOS Keychain into a password manager. This is open since 17 Oct, because it is the only way to decrypt the backups if the Mac is lost.

- **Telegram delivery check.** The user is asked to visually confirm the two daily messages (CV and Arabic) in topic 35 of the Digmi Laboratorium group. Scheduled sends failed on 17 Oct because python-telegram-bot was missing; the assistant installed it, but a clean scheduled run is not yet confirmed.

- **Hindsight reboot test.** A full cold-start test is pending. Only launchctl bootstrap has been tested.

- **Azure Storage Explorer.** Azure AD sign-in on the arm64 build is not verified end to end as of 18 Oct. The Quick Access list needs re-pinning.

- **Thesis (MTI, BINUS University).** The proposal is complete and the outline is in progress. No formal deadline is recorded. In Feb 2026 the user estimated about six months of working time remained. The OCR of the 19-page guideline is saved at /Users/imamtaufiq/Workspace/thesis/BINUS_unlimited_ocr_8bit.md.

## Recurring commitments the user has set up

- 03:00 hermes-settings-backup (no-agent mode, Telegram report of short statistics). 03:05 hindsight-memory-backup. 21:20 dotfiles-backup.

- 09:00 Computer Vision lesson and 09:05 Arabic Dars Yaum lesson, both to Telegram topic 35. The CV lesson is one concept per day; the last one covered was digital image representation (17 Oct), and the next is convolution. Arabic lessons also cover one daily 'ammiyah expression and a speaking challenge.

- Every 7 days: Arabic grammar review (nahwu and sharf).

- Schedule conflict: on 17 Oct the user asked for 21:00, 21:05 and 21:15. Later records (17 Oct 13:56 and 19 Oct) show 09:00, 09:05 and 03:00/03:05/21:20. The later records are treated as current, but it is not recorded whether the learning jobs were reverted to 21:00, so the user should confirm.

- Weekly or periodic: brain-vault compile (Obsidian LLM Wiki). Time not recorded.

## Notes on how to follow up

- Telegram is the user's primary channel. Scheduled job reports go there, and failures must always surface.

- The user wants candid uncertainty over invented answers, and prefers concrete, direct, specific communication. Given the earlier laptop failure and data loss, reliable backup reporting matters a great deal to the user.
